newsitem.title: USA: Judge to issue ruling on Hilton motion soon.
newsitem.headline: Judge to issue ruling on Hilton motion soon.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp on Wednesday said a judge was expected to issue a decision soon on two key motions in Hilton's $6.5 billion hostile takeover bid for rival ITT Corp.

The motions, which seek to prevent ITT from increasing the size of its board of directors or interfering with the board election process, were discussed during an hour-long hearing here in front of U.S. District Court Judge Philip Pro on Wednesday.
Hilton spokesman Marc Grossman said the judge told both sides he planned to issue a ruling shortly.

Hilton offered to acquire ITT in January for a combination of cash and stock worth $6.5 billion. Hilton also offered to assume $4 billion in debt, bringing the total value of the deal to $10.5 billion.
ITT rejected the bid and has embarked on a programme to shed non-core assets in an effort to raise cash and perhaps offer shareholders a special dividend.

Hilton, which has proposed 25 nominees to ITT's board of directors, is asking the court to prevent ITT from increasing its board beyond the current 11 directors. If the judge rules in Hilton's favour, the company stands a better chance of getting sympathetic directors on ITT's board, something Hilton will need if ITT continues to oppose a merger.
The Beverly Hills, Calif.-based hotel and gaming giant is also trying to prevent ITT from adopting a poison pill, which would make a takeover more expensive.
In a separate motion, Hilton has asked the court to force ITT to hold it annual meeting in May. The judge is expected to hear arguments from both sides on that motion later.
